title: waitForStage double-releases the job semaphore when a remote build's context is cancelled (panic: semaphore: released more than held)
body:
### Issue Description

`imagebuildah.(*executor).waitForStage` yields the job semaphore and then fails to reacquire it when the build context is cancelled. The stage goroutine's `defer stagesSemaphore.Release(1)` then panics:

```
panic: semaphore: released more than held
```

When that executor is running inside `podman system service` (the user-scope API socket), the panic kills the whole API server. Socket activation starts a fresh instance that knows nothing of other in-flight remote builds on the same socket, so those clients die with `Error: server probably quit: unexpected EOF`.

This is still present on buildah `main` (`imagebuildah/executor.go` is identical to v1.45.0 at the semaphore sites). It is not fixed in any released podman; latest is 6.1.1, which vendors buildah 1.45.0.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Requires a **remote** `podman build` through `podman system service` (not a local `podman build`). Two clients on the same API socket:

1. Start the user-scope API server (`systemctl --user start podman.socket`; `CONTAINER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$UID/podman/podman.sock`).
2. Start a remote build of a Containerfile with a long `RUN` (several minutes).
3. While that `RUN` is in flight, kill the **client** (SIGINT / close the connection). Do not wait for a clean server-side cancel.
4. Immediately start a second remote build through the same socket.

### Describe the results you received

The API server panics a short time after the cancelled client's in-flight `RUN` finishes:

```
panic: semaphore: released more than held
    vendor/golang.org/x/sync/semaphore/semaphore.go:136
    go.podman.io/buildah/imagebuildah.(*executor).Build.func3.1()
    vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/imagebuildah/executor.go:1187
```

`podman.service` exits status 2; systemd socket-activates a new server. The second build dies with:

```
Error: server probably quit: unexpected EOF
```

Observed live 2026-09-07 on Homebrew podman 6.1.1 (buildah 1.45.0) serving three GitHub Actions heavy-slot builds through one user-scope socket. Cancelling a superseded CI run (GitHub `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true`) disconnected the first client and took down the next run's build on another slot.

### Describe the results you expected

The cancelled build is torn down on the server side. Other remote builds on the same API server are unaffected. The executor must not panic.

### buildah version output

```
Vendored in podman 6.1.1: buildah 1.45.0
Compared against buildah main on 2026-09-08: imagebuildah/executor.go is unchanged at the semaphore sites (lines 515-541 waitForStage, 1136 Acquire, 1150 defer Release).
```

### buildah info output

```
Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (WSL2), linux/amd64, cgroup v2, crun 1.29.1
podman: 6.1.1 (brew, Go 1.27.1, built 2026-09-02)
API: user-scope unix:///run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock
graphDriver: overlay
graphRoot: /home/dev/.local/share/containers/storage
runRoot: /run/user/1001/containers
```

### Provide your storage.conf

Default Homebrew podman storage (overlay). Not implicated; the panic is in the job-semaphore accounting, not storage.

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes — reproduced on podman 6.1.1 / buildah 1.45.0 (latest releases as of 2026-09-08). Confirmed the same code is still on buildah `main`.

### Additional environment details

WSL2 host. Several GitHub Actions runner containers share one `podman system service` over a bind-mounted user socket (`CONTAINER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock`). The panic is in buildah; sharing one API server is what turns a single cancelled build into a host-wide outage.

### Additional information

**Mechanism.** `Build` acquires one job-semaphore token per stage goroutine and `defer Release(1)`s it (`executor.go:1136, 1150`). `waitForStage` yields that token while polling another stage:

```go
b.stagesSemaphore.Release(1)
time.Sleep(time.Millisecond * 10)
if err := b.stagesSemaphore.Acquire(ctx, 1); err != nil {
    return true, fmt.Errorf("reacquiring job semaphore: %w", err)
}
```

If `ctx` is cancelled (remote client gone), `Acquire` fails and `waitForStage` returns **without** holding a token. `buildStage` then returns the error, and the goroutine's `defer Release(1)` panics (`cur < 0`).

The stack line `executor.go:1187` is the `return` after `stageErr != nil` — that is when the deferred `Release` runs.

**Suggested fix.** If the reacquire fails, take the token back with a non-cancelled context so the outer `defer Release` stays balanced:

```go
b.stagesSemaphore.Release(1)
time.Sleep(time.Millisecond * 10)
if err := b.stagesSemaphore.Acquire(ctx, 1); err != nil {
    if err2 := b.stagesSemaphore.Acquire(context.Background(), 1); err2 != nil {
        return true, fmt.Errorf("reacquiring job semaphore: %w (then %w)", err, err2)
    }
    return true, fmt.Errorf("reacquiring job semaphore: %w", err)
}
```

Happy to open a PR if that shape is acceptable.

**Related second panic** (separate nil-deref, same cancel path, also kills `podman system service`):

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
    go.podman.io/buildah/imagebuildah.(*stageExecutor).getContentSummaryAfterAddingContent
        stage_executor.go:1270
```

`s.builder` is nil when `ContentDigester.Digest()` is called. Observed twice on the same host after the semaphore panic, 2026-09-07 13:05 and 13:08. A semaphore-only fix would not cover this path.

comments.body: Working on a PR for this. I'll include a unit test that fails on the cancelled-context reacquire path and a nil-guard for the related `getContentSummaryAfterAddingContent` deref we saw on the same cancel path.
